_comment: How WFP's Libya food-price CSV on HDX maps onto this country's configuration.
Read by infra/scripts/wfp-hdx-import.py, which turns the CSV into a file
PartnerFileImporter accepts. Everything country-specific about that
transformation lives here, not in the script (constraint C3).
`markets` is WFP's spelling of each market it surveys, against the slug
of the configured location it is. Recovered on 3 September 2026 by
matching the 2,348 rows already imported against the CSV: every one of
the fifteen agrees cell for cell. Six WFP markets — Algatroun, Aljufra,
Alkufra, Nalut, Wadi Alshati, Zwara — have no configured location and
are dropped on purpose rather than forced onto a neighbour. Gharyan is
configured but WFP's 'Ghiryan' series ends before 2024.
`commodities` lists the WFP series that price a basket item, with the
unit code and quantity the importer must be told, because WFP's own unit
strings ('KG', '30 pcs', 'L') are not configured units. `code` is the
catalogue item the series is expected to resolve to; the script uses it
only to skip rows already imported, never to bypass the matcher.
Series WFP still carries but stopped collecting are listed under
`stale` with their last month, so nobody re-discovers them as coverage:
the inventory in docs/data-sources.md counted them as priceable and the
file says otherwise.
